# Adversarial Design Review: SiriusXM macOS Client

Verdict first: **blockers exist. Design not merge-ready as proposed.** Biggest issues: loopback proxy session-hijack surface, token-in-URL leaking into system telemetry by construction, no specified redaction barrier, no rate-limit budget, and one feature (webview session extraction) that must be dropped or re-scoped.

---

## 1. Credential-at-rest (Keychain)

**[HIGH] `kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked` + `kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain:true` is the right skeleton, but the plan as stated has three holes.**

- Risk 1: `kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain:true` gives iOS-style per-app keychain. Fine. But nothing specifies *what* gets stored. If the plan stores username+password to support silent re-auth, that is a standing credential on disk that any code in the app's keychain access group can read. Store only the short-lived Bearer token + gupId. Never the password. If silent re-auth needs a refresh credential, store the *session cookie/refresh token*, not the password.
- Risk 2: keychain survives uninstall. After reinstall, app finds a stale token for a possibly different account. This is a correctness bug, not just UX: wrong account's gupId can be sent to the API, which looks like account sharing to SiriusXM's abuse detection. Remediation: on first launch after install (detect via absence of a UserDefaults install marker), delete any pre-existing keychain items before use. Test: integration test that pre-seeds keychain, deletes marker file, asserts cleanup.
- Risk 3: Touch-ID gating (`kSecAttrAccessControl` with `.userPresence`) is mentioned as a question, not a decision. Decide: **no biometric gate.** Streaming apps re-read tokens on every refresh cycle; user-presence prompts on background token refresh will train users to click through, and failed prompts in headless/background contexts cause silent playback death. Use `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` instead — `ThisDeviceOnly` blocks keychain-backup/Migration-Assistant exfiltration of the token to another Mac. That flag is the verifiable rule: code review grep for `kSecAttrAccessible` must show `AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, nothing else.

**[MEDIUM] Token expiry handling unspecified.** If expired token is retried against the media URL, Akamai returns 403 storms. Remediation: proactive refresh at expiry − 60s, single-flight refresh (one in-flight refresh per process, others await), hard circuit breaker after 2 consecutive 401/403s → re-auth flow, not retry.

---

## 2. Loopback proxy (option B)

Plain sentence because this is the security-critical section: **I recommend dropping option B.** It adds a permanent network listener to solve a problem option A solves in-process, and every hardening requirement below is a corner a rushed implementer will cut. If the team insists on B for AVPlayer compatibility reasons, all of the following are merge gates:

- **[CRITICAL] Session hijack by local processes.** Any process running as the same user (or root) can connect to `127.0.0.1:<port>` and request `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...` — the proxy will happily append `?consumer=k2&token=...&gupId=...` and proxy it, handing a live session token to any local malware or curious process. Ephemeral port is not a defense; port-scanning 64k ports on localhost takes under a second. Remediation: per-launch unguessable path prefix (`/<128-bit-random-uuid>/manifest.m3u8`), proxy 404s anything outside it, and only URLs containing the prefix are ever handed to AVPlayer. Test: unit test asserts requests without prefix get 404 and no upstream call.
- **[HIGH] Peer-credential check.** On multi-user Macs, other *users* can also connect to 127.0.0.1. Random path helps but is observable via `lsof`/process inspection by same-user processes. Stronger: `SO_PEERCRED`-equivalent on macOS (`getpeereid` on the accept socket is not available for TCP; use `proc_pidfdinfo` audit or accept only connections whose peer is same-UID via `getpeereid` on a **Unix domain socket** instead of TCP). Unix socket in a 0700 directory kills the multi-user and (mostly) cross-user problem outright. Rule: if proxy ships, it must be a Unix domain socket, not TCP loopback. AVPlayer can't speak UDS directly — this alone is the argument for option A.
- **[HIGH] DNS rebinding / browser confusion.** A malicious web page open in the user's browser can `fetch("http://127.0.0.1:port/...")`. CORS blocks reading the response, but the *request still fires* — the proxy can't tell browser-origin traffic from AVPlayer. Remediation: require a custom header AVFoundation sends (`X-Playback-Session-ID` from `AVURLAsset` options) or the random path prefix; 403 on any request with an `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch-*` header (browsers always send those, AVPlayer never does). Test: send request with `Origin: https://evil.example`, assert 403.
- **[MEDIUM] Token in rewritten manifest URLs.** Rewritten playlists contain `token=...` in plaintext and get handed to AVPlayer, which surfaces current-item URLs in `AVPlayerItem.errorLog()`, `AccessLog`, and sysdiagnose. Mitigation: token never appears in URLs the proxy *serves* — proxy holds token in memory keyed by the random path, injects query params only on the upstream (outbound) request. Downstream manifest keeps the local URL. This also fixes caching. Rule: grep-test that no generated local URL contains `token=`.
- **[LOW] Port exhaustion / second instance.** Handle multiple app instances: per-instance socket path, no shared state.

---

## 3. Resource loader (option A) — preferred, with caveats

- **[HIGH] `AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate` breaks HTTP caching and byte-range semantics if implemented naively.** HLS variants, redirects, and `contentInformationRequest` (etag, length, range support) must be filled correctly or seeking/live-DVR windows break and every segment refetches. Remediation: implement `loadingRequest.contentInformationRequest` fully (contentLength, isByteRangeAccessSupported=true), pass through `If-None-Match`/206 responses. Test: integration test on a recorded playlist asserting Range requests and 206 pass-through.
- **[MEDIUM] System telemetry still sees the final URL.** With option A, all requests go through `URLSession` inside mediaserverd-equivalent machinery (actually the app's own session for resource loader — media requests come into *your process*, which is an advantage). But if you inject the token by redirect/rewritten URL and that URL ever lands in `NSError` descriptions, `os_log`, or `MetricKit` payloads, it exfiltrates. Same redaction rule as §4.
- **[MEDIUM] Key/fairplay-adjacent requests.** AAC HLS uses `EXT-X-KEY` with `METHOD=AES-128` — key URLs also need the token appended, and resource loader must handle `skd:`/relative URL schemes. Missed key-URL rewriting = silent playback failure, not an error. Test: playlist fixture with AES-128 key tag; assert key request carries token.
- **[LOW] interstitial/ad segments** from Akamai may carry their own query strings — append, don't replace, when injecting params. Naive `URL + "?token="` on a URL already having `?` produces a broken URL.

Decision: **ship A, drop B.** A keeps credentials in-process, has no listener, no rebinding surface. B's only real advantage is letting AVPlayer do its own networking; the cost is an entire hardening program.

---

## 4. Log/analytics exfiltration

Enumerate escape paths, then the gate:

1. `os_log` / `Logger` — default privacy is your friend only if every `\(url)` interpolation is `.private` or a custom `TokenRedacting` wrapper. One raw interpolation leaks to Console and sysdiagnose.
2. `print`/`debugPrint` — goes to stdout attached to Xcode/Console, and into crash report "Application Specific Information" only if explicitly set — still ban in protocol module.
3. **Crash reports**: URLs live in `NSError.userInfo[NSURLErrorFailingURLKey]` and appear in stack-adjacent strings. Wrap errors in a domain error that carries a *redacted* URL only.
4. `UserDefaults` — nothing with `token`, `gupId`, cookie values ever written. Rule: review grep.
5. **User-visible error alerts** — users screenshot/copy-paste them into GitHub issues. Alert text must never contain query strings. Show a short code (`AUTH_EXPIRED`) plus redacted host only.
6. MetricKit/os_trace signposts with URL payload.
7. GitHub issue templates — add a checklist line: "remove any tokens from logs before attaching" *and* make logs incapable of containing them (see below).

**Verifiable gate (the test that enforces this):** a `RedactingURL`/`SensitiveString` type whose `CustomStringConvertible`/`Codable` output is always `<redacted:sha256prefix>`. Protocol module may not use bare `URL`/`String` for session material — enforced by a lint rule (swiftlint custom rule or source-scan test) that fails the build if `os_log`, `Logger`, `print` appear in the protocol module, or if `token|gupId` appear in any `UserDefaults`, `NSAlert`, or error-`userInfo` construction. Plus one fuzz test: run a full auth+playback cycle against a mock server, capture every log emit and error object via a custom log collector, assert the raw token string appears nowhere.

---

## 5. WebView (option B auth)

**[HIGH — bad idea as frameable] Extracting the session from a WKWebView by scripting/cookie-observation crosses a line.** Reading tokens out of a webview the user logged into is functionally credential interception of a first-party session against the provider's JS sandbox. It also likely violates SiriusXM ToS and, if done via injected JavaScript, mimics the provider's own client in a way that weakens any "interoperability" defense. **Drop silent JS token extraction.** Acceptable scope: webview used only for the interactive login page (to handle CAPTCHA/MFA the user solves themselves), then read *only* the documented session artifacts via `WKHTTPCookieStore` observation of the specific session cookie on the specific domain — same mechanism a browser extension with user consent uses. No `evaluateJavaScript` scraping, no keylog-adjacent handlers, no `WKScriptMessageHandler` receiving page data.

- **[MEDIUM] Script message handlers**: if any `WKUserContentController.add(_, name:)` exists, it's an injection bridge from SiriusXM's page (or a MITM'd page) into app code. Rule: zero script message handlers. Enforce by source-scan.
- **[MEDIUM] Navigation**: `WKNavigationDelegate` must hard-allowlist `*.siriusxm.com` (exact suffix match with dot boundary — `siriusxm.com.evil.tld` must fail), cancel everything else, open externally. Set `limitsNavigationsToAppBoundDomains = true` where possible.
- **[MEDIUM] `nonPersistent()` data store**: correct choice for disk persistence, but note it keeps cookies **in memory for the webview's lifetime** — long-lived webview = long-lived exfil window. Destroy webview and data store immediately after session establishment.
- **[LOW] `nonPersistent` does not isolate Keychain autofill** — Safari password autofill isn't available in non-safari-view webviews anyway, so no keychain-persistence issue, but document password-field autofill behavior (`textContentType`) so the macOS credential provider flow works.
- Prefer programmatic auth (option A) with a **webview fallback only for CAPTCHA/MFA**, and never store the password (per §1).

---

## 6. Legal/ToS

Not legal advice; engineering-risk assessment:

**Unacceptable — do not build, these create CFAA/DMCA-1201/ToS exposure:**
- Any DRM bypass or capture of the decrypted audio path (screen-recording-grade capture of AVPlayer output is a different feature — leave it out).
- CAPTCHA/MFA bypass or automated solving. User-solves-only.
- Device-limit / concurrent-stream circumvention (e.g., spoofing device IDs to exceed stream caps, gupId rotation to dodge limits).
- Credential interception beyond first-party session establishment (§5).
- Resharing/rebroadcasting, recording-to-disk feature.

**Defensible:**
- User's own paid subscription, one stream, user-initiated auth.
- Read-only use of APIs the user's own browser session already calls.
- Clear README disclosure: unofficial, not affiliated, no warranty, credentials stored locally only, no telemetry to third parties.
- Weakest points honestly: automated login against unofficial endpoints is still ToS-gray regardless of cleanliness, and SiriusXM can break or block it anytime — design must degrade gracefully, not retaliate with evasion. Any "rotate device ID on 403" logic is an evasion tell: ban it by rule.

**Verifiable rule:** source-scan test banning hardcoded alternate device IDs, user agents other than a single declared one, and any retry-on-block logic that varies request fingerprints.

---

## 7. Supply chain

- Zero third-party runtime deps is a good rule — **keep it absolute**, including "just" a keychain wrapper or "just" SwiftNIO for the proxy. Each one is a precompiled-binary or unpinned-version risk. This is another strike against option B (temptation to pull in a server framework).
- No analytics/crash SDKs (Sentry, Firebase, Crashlytics) — they are token exfiltration paths you don't control (§4).
- Dev-only deps (linters) must never be linked into the app target; pin `Package.resolved`, CI verifies no unexpected URL appears in resolved file (allowlist: github.com/apple/* only, if any).
- Enable library validation / hardened runtime for the signed app; no `disable-library-validation` entitlement. Entitlements audit in CI: diff entitlements plist against committed baseline.

---

## 8. Quality risks in the delivery plan

- **Untestable as scoped**: "playback works" against live SiriusXM is not a test. Gate: `resources/` fixtures of recorded playlists (master, variant, AES-128, ad interstitial, 403-expired-token) + playback-state integration tests against a local stub server. No live-network test in the default suite.
- **Silently rots**: unofficial API drifts. Need a contract canary — a CI job (not in merge path) hitting the real endpoints weekly, alerting on schema change. Without it, first user discovers breakage.
- **Module boundary** ("UI never imports protocol module") must be enforced by SwiftPM target topology (separate targets, protocol types `internal` where possible), not convention — otherwise schedule pressure erases it. Test: build-graph check / a source-scan asserting `import ProtocolModule` absent from UI target.
- **"Done" criteria too weak anywhere auth and token-lifecycle are concerned.** Minimum: expired-token mid-stream recovery test, 403→single re-auth→no-storm test, keychain-cleanup-on-reinstall test, redaction fuzz (§4), logout-purges-keychain-and-memory test.
- Swift 6 strict concurrency: resource loader callbacks cross isolation domains; require `Sendable` audit on the protocol module and CI with `-strict-concurrency=complete`. Data race in token cache is the classic corner-cut here.

---

## 9. Rate limiting / account safety

- **[HIGH] Unbounded retry = account ban.** Design has no stated retry budget. Requirements, all testable:
  - Auth endpoints: max 3 attempts, exponential backoff 2s/10s/60s, then user-facing stop. Never auto-retry password auth on 401.
  - Token refresh: single-flight, at most 1 refresh per 30s process-wide.
  - Media 403/401: circuit breaker (§1), one token refresh, then halt playback with clear error — not a retry loop.
  - Global token-bucket on all edge-gateway calls (e.g., 60/min); log (redacted) when bucket refused.
  - Respect `Retry-After` exactly; jittered backoff otherwise.
  - **Test**: mock server returning 403; assert ≤ N total requests in 60s window and that fingerprint (headers/device id) is identical across retries.
- **[MEDIUM] Background refresh**: no polling while app idle/closed beyond what playback needs; continuous manifest revalidation against a paused stream is an abuse signal.

---

## Blocker checklist (all must be yes before any code merge)

- [ ] Loopback proxy dropped **or** all §2 gates implemented (prefer drop).
- [ ] Keychain: `AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, no password stored, stale-item cleanup on reinstall.
- [ ] `RedactingURL` type + lint gate: no `os_log`/`print`/`UserDefaults`/alert/error-userInfo usage with raw session material; redaction fuzz test.
- [ ] Zero script message handlers in webview; domain allowlist with dot-boundary match; no JS session scraping.
- [ ] Retry budget per §9 with fingerprint-stable retries; circuit breaker test.
- [ ] Module boundary enforced by SwiftPM targets + import-scan test.
- [ ] Playlist fixtures + stub-server integration tests incl. AES-128 key, Range/206, 403 paths.
- [ ] No third-party runtime deps; `Package.resolved` allowlist; entitlements baseline in CI.
- [ ] README legal disclosure; no device-limit/recording/evasion features, banned-by-source-scan.

Thin hand-written .xcodeproj deferred to the final packaging phase only (SwiftPM executableTarget emits no .app bundle). Module split: SiriusXMCore (pure value types, zero I/O) / SiriusXMProtocol (only place that knows hosts+tokens+JSON keys) / SiriusXMNet (URLSession transport) / SiriusXMPlayback (owns AVPlayer, receives opaque MediaHandoff so tokens never cross) / SiriusXMUI (SwiftUI + @Observable) / SiriusXMApp (sole @MainActor composition root). Enforce UI-never-imports-protocol via SwiftPM target topology + source-scan test, not convention.

SiriusXM macOS app — protocol reality. The old "jam endpoints + HMAC-SHA1 listener + MP3" protocol in common tutorials is DEAD/unverified; those repos (mattsch/siriusxm-radio, mihaigalos/libSiriusXM, krateng/jupox, krateng/siriusxm-player) now 404. Two live generations: (1) edge gateway Bearer token at api.edge-gateway.siriusxm.com with POST /playback/play/v1/tuneSource body {type:"channel-linear",hlsVersion:"V3",manifestVariant:"WEB"}; media on live-*.streaming.siriusxm.com; token acquisition is UNKNOWN. (2) Legacy cookie web-player API player.siriusxm.com/rest/v2/experience/modules/* with SXMAUTH/SXMAKTOKEN/SXMDATA.gupId cookies — shape stable 2015→2026, good fallback. Audio is HLS/AAC from Akamai, Content-Type audio/x-aac, NOT MP3. tuneSource returns trackResumeSupported:false so all timeshift must be client-side. Media requests need ?consumer=k2&token=...&gupId=... appended — segment URLs carry no creds. Closest prior art: gabeosx/canis97 (shipping macOS SwiftUI player, MIT). Protocol layout must distinguish CONFIRMED vs INFERRED vs UNKNOWN; never invent endpoint names.

SiriusXM macOS app — macOS 14 audio gotchas. AVAudioSession does NOT exist on macOS (iOS/tvOS/watchOS only) — most common iOS-port mistake. Output routing, AirPods, route changes are free behind AVPlayer/CoreAudio. For device loss use the CoreAudio default-output-device HAL property listener, not interruption notifications. macOS has NO background-audio execution mode and no entitlement for one; handle NSWorkspace didSleep/didWake (suspend player, re-resolve on wake). No Synchronization.Mutex (macOS 15+), no AsyncTimerSequence (macOS 15+) — use NSLock/OSAllocatedUnfairLock and Task.sleep loops. @Observable available on macOS 14. MPNowPlayingInfoPropertyIsLiveStream=true makes Control Center suppress the scrubber — pick honest live (skip buttons only) vs dishonest clock. skipForwardCommand.preferredIntervals must be a multiple of measured HLS segment duration or seeks stall mid-segment.

Timeshift/replay clock pattern for live HLS. Do NOT build a ring buffer unless measurement proves the CDN HLS window <5 min — the rolling playlist window IS the DVR window, exposed as AVPlayerItem.seekableTimeRanges. Never compute replay offset from Date() vs #EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME: an NTP jump teleports the user. Use anchor-and-delta: store PlaybackAnchor{itemTime, wallClock}, offset = CMTimeGetSeconds(currentTime - anchor.itemTime), pure monotonic CMTime math. Re-anchor on tune, seek, resume-live, sleep/wake, network recovery — never on a timer tick. If a buffer is ever needed, buffer COMPRESSED segments not PCM (AAC@128k = 28MB/30min vs 690MB Float32). Surface behind-live-edge with a ● LIVE button; never auto-yank the user forward. Jump to live via seek(to: .positiveInfinity).

SiriusXM macOS app — UI/UX direction. macOS 14+ HIG-native, no third-party UI, no custom fonts. Single main window, NavigationSplitView with 280pt sidebar (materials: .sidebar / .regular / .sheet), min size 980x640, full-height traffic lights, unified toolbar. Sidebar surfaces: Now Playing, Guide (grouped by genre, collapsible), Favorites, Search, Settings. Now Playing: album art 320pt (240pt on narrow), 16pt radius, shadow radius 4; metadata stack Channel 17 Semibold / Track title 20 Semibold / Artist 15 / time-remaining 13; transport 28/48/28pt with backward.end, play.fill, pause.fill, forward.end, 24pt gaps, 44pt hit targets. 8pt spacing grid, 8pt controls / 12pt cards / 16pt art corner radii. Channel brand color tints controls only, never backgrounds. Dark-first system materials. Motion: 0.25s spring play/pause morph, 0.3s art crossfade, 2s Live pulse — all disabled under Reduce Motion. MenuBarExtra + MPRemoteCommandCenter/Control Center Now Playing widget. Keyboard: Space play/pause, arrows seek, Cmd-F search. Eight states must be designed: signed out, idle, live, replay, buffering, network lost, channel offline, empty favorites, no search results. Error copy rule: one title, one sentence, one button; never show a raw code, URL, or HTTP status. Compatibility & Support screen shows six ordered stages (Authentication, Entitlement, Catalog, Stream resolution, Metadata, Native playback) each unavailable vs not-yet-run — this stops users pasting tokens into GitHub issues.

# Design brief — native macOS SiriusXM app

**Repo empty.** Only `.gitignore` + `LICENSE` (Apache 2.0), one init commit, remote `github.com/rileycalhoun/siriusxm-macos`. Greenfield. Nothing written.

**Blocked on you:** kane cannot `scp` or `git clone`. Every build gate needs a human copy of the tree into `~/SandboxBuilds/<name>` on kane first. Probes returned `DENIED: not permitted by the xcodebuild sandbox.` Phase 0 is un-runnable until you do that.

## What it looks like

Single main window, `NavigationSplitView`, 280pt sidebar, min 980×640, full-height traffic lights, `.windowBackgroundMaterial`. Sidebar: Now Playing, Guide (genres, collapsible), Favorites, Search, Settings.

Now Playing centers on art (320pt, 16pt radius, shadow radius 4) over a metadata stack — channel 17 Semibold, track title 20 Semibold, artist 15, offset 13. Transport28/48/28pt, 44pt hit targets. 8pt spacing grid. Channel brand color tints controls only, never backgrounds. Menu bar extra + Control Center Now Playing. Space/arrows/Cmd-F.

Eight states designed up front, not afterthoughts: signed out, idle, live, replay, buffering, offline, channel off-air, empty favorites, no search results.

## What it does

AVPlayer on HLS/AAC. **No ring buffer** — the rolling playlist window *is* the DVR window, via `seekableTimeRanges`. Replay offset computed anchor-and-delta on monotonic `CMTime`, never `Date()` minus program-date-time, or an NTP jump teleports the user. Never auto-yank forward to live.

Protocol reality, corrected: the "jam endpoints + HMAC-SHA1 + MP3" tutorials are dead. Two live generations — Bearer edge gateway at `api.edge-gateway.siriusxm.com`, and the2015-era cookie web-player API at `player.siriusxm.com` (shape stable 11 years, good fallback). Audio is AAC from Akamai. Token acquisition is UNKNOWN; resolve it live early. Prior art to study: `gabeosx/canis97`.

## Security verdict — QA blocked it as proposed

Loopback proxy option **dropped**. It hands a live session token to any process running as the same user; ephemeral ports are not a defense. Ship `AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate` — no listener, no hijack surface. Fill `contentInformationRequest` fully or Range/206 semantics break seeking.

Keychain: `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, never the password, stale-item cleanup on reinstall (a stale gupId sent to the API reads as account sharing). No biometric gate — a Touch-ID prompt on every background token refresh teaches users to click through.

`RedactingURL` type whose description and `Codable` are always `<redacted:…>`, plus a source-scan test failing the build if `os_log`/`print` appears in the protocol module or `token|gupId` reaches `UserDefaults`/alerts/error userInfo. Tokens live in `NSURLErrorFailingURLKey` and ride into crash reports.

WebView: login page only, user solves their own CAPTCHA/MFA, read only the documented session cookie. Zero script message handlers, no JS scraping.

Retry budget is an account-safety matter, not a nicety: auth max 3 with2s/10s/60s backoff, single-flight refresh, global token bucket, fingerprint-stable retries. Unbounded retry against a rate-limited service gets the subscriber's account flagged.

Banned by source-scan: device-limit circumvention, recording, DRM bypass, third-party runtime deps.
